snippet.title: The Dark-Web Market Police Secretly Controlled
snippet.description:
When Dutch police secretly took over Hansa, buyers kept using the dark-web market without knowing who was in control. The operation recorded more than 50,000 transactions before the site was shut down in 2017.

snippet.title: How a Car Manual Publisher Ended Up Publishing Dune
snippet.description:
Oregon’s shifting sand dunes led Frank Herbert to study how beachgrass held sand in place, helping inspire the desert world of Arrakis. After publishers rejected *Dune*, Chilton, a company known for car-repair manuals, agreed to publish it.

snippet.title: Did People Really Think Birds Flew to the Moon?
snippet.description:
In the 17th century, Charles Morton suggested that swallows and storks wintered on the Moon. On May 21, 1822, a white stork shot near Klütz carried an 80-centimeter arrow from Central Africa in its neck, becoming the first physical evidence of long-distance migration among European birds.
